root_cause.text: In `fs/smb/client/smb2file.c`’s `symlink_data()` loop, `p->ErrorDataLength` was used to advance to the next SMB2 error context without validating that the aligned length stayed within the remaining buffer, allowing crafted 32-bit values to wrap pointer arithmetic and cause an infinite loop or out-of-bounds read.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (len > end - ((u8 *)p + sizeof(*p))) return ERR_PTR(-EINVAL);` immediately before `p = (struct smb2_error_context_rsp *)(p->ErrorContextData + len);`, and the CVE describes exact 32-bit cases where `ErrorDataLength` makes `p + len` equal `p` (loop) or `(u8 *)p - 8` (OOB read).

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a bounds check in SMB2 symlink error parsing to reject truncated or malformed error context data.
intent_record.what: In symlink_data(), after computing len as ALIGN(le32_to_cpu(p->ErrorDataLength), 8), the code now checks whether len exceeds the remaining buffer space from the current error context pointer to end; if so, it returns ERR_PTR(-EINVAL) before advancing p to the next smb2_error_context_rsp.
intent_record.how: This prevents the parser from walking past the end of the received SMB2 error response when ErrorDataLength is malformed or truncated, avoiding out-of-bounds access and rejecting invalid input with -EINVAL.
